prompts.duo:
Create a 15-second photorealistic vertical 9:16 studio rap duet with synchronized sound.

REFERENCE ROLES AND PRIORITY
Image 1 defines performer A's identity, facial structure, hair, skin tone and visible clothing. Image 2 defines performer B's identity and visible clothing. These two portraits are the exclusive sources of human appearance. Image 3 defines the empty teal-green cyclorama studio, soft lighting, low oval riser and single silver hanging microphone. Image 4 is a neutral gray-mannequin reference for the opening two-shot, left-right placement and small arm gestures. Image 5 is a neutral gray-mannequin reference for B's close-up and the microphone at the left edge. Replace the mannequin bodies completely with A and B, with natural skin, facial details and the clothing from their own portraits. Copy camera composition and approximate poses from Images 4 and 5 only. Keep exactly two real performers and one microphone.

IDENTITY AND SPATIAL CONTINUITY
A stays on screen-left and B stays on screen-right throughout. Keep each face, hairstyle and outfit attached to the same person through turns, occlusion and cuts. The camera stays on one side of the action axis. The silver microphone hangs vertically on one thin black cable between them. It stays suspended and stationary as the two performers exchange their singing roles. Preserve the teal floor, curved seamless background and low riser across all shots. The portraits determine clothes and accessories; complete unseen lower-body clothing consistently.

SHOT AND PERFORMANCE TIMELINE
0.0-3.5 seconds: Waist-up two-shot using Image 4's composition. A performs the opening hook phrase heard in Audio 1, with small rhythmic forearm gestures and natural facial expression. B listens, nods and smiles with relaxed closed lips during A's words.
3.5-5.0 seconds: Continue the two-shot. A finishes the hook and turns slightly toward B. B turns toward A to take the next vocal phrase. Keep A left and B right, with a brief conversational handoff. Align the exact mouth opening and handoff to Audio 1.
5.0-8.7 seconds: Cut to B's close-up, following Image 5's camera position. B performs the verse in Audio 1. Keep the silver mic near the left edge, B's identity clear, natural blinking, precise mouth articulation and one compact gesture near chest level.
8.7-11.5 seconds: Cut to a full-body wide shot revealing A left and B right on the low oval teal riser. B continues the verse; A grooves lightly with small shoulder movements. Keep their feet planted naturally and both bodies proportionate.
11.5-15.0 seconds: Return to a medium two-shot from the same side of the axis. B finishes the remaining audible vocal phrase while A reacts with a warm smile. Both share an amused look on the final beat. During any audible singing, keep the assigned singer lip-synced; use smiles or a light laugh only in the available pauses. End at 15 seconds.

AUDIO AND LIP-SYNC
Use Audio 1 as the reference for the existing words, vocal phrasing, singer handoff, rhythm, backing track and pauses. Follow its language, syllable timing and delivery closely. A performs the opening hook and B performs the later verse. Maintain the reference audio's musical continuity through every camera cut. Prioritize the audible phrasing when fine-tuning the approximate shot times above. Preserve the reference lyrics without adding, translating or rewriting lines, new narration or extra sung parts. Produce synchronized native audio for this generation; the result will be reviewed as returned by the model.

QUALITY CONSTRAINTS
Keep identities and clothing stable. Avoid face swaps, duplicate people, mannequin material, featureless faces, body morphing, extra fingers or limbs, microphone duplication and abrupt background changes. The studio remains a simple teal cyclorama with one riser and one hanging mic. Use clean realistic skin detail, gentle studio shadows and restrained performance motion. Keep the frame free of captions, logos, watermarks and on-screen text.

The adult stays screen-left and the pet stays screen-right. Both occupy the same low oval teal riser. The pet sits or stands naturally on its own paws at its real scale. Keep the microphone stationary on its hanging cable above their shared performance space, with framing adjusted to show the pet clearly. Maintain the adult's outfit and the pet's fur through every cut. Keep all camera viewpoints on one side of the action axis.

0.0-3.5 seconds: Medium two-shot showing the adult and pet. The adult delivers the opening hook from Audio 1 with small hand gestures. The pet watches with subtle head tilts and a calm natural pose.
3.5-5.0 seconds: The adult finishes the hook and turns toward the pet with an inviting smile. The pet raises its attention toward the microphone while remaining screen-right. Align the handoff to the actual vocal transition in Audio 1.
5.0-8.7 seconds: Cut to the pet's close-up, with the silver mic near the left edge. The pet performs the later vocal phrase as a gentle fictional speaking-animal effect. Use subtle rhythmic jaw and lip movement while preserving the animal's muzzle, teeth, eyes and species-specific facial structure.
8.7-11.5 seconds: Cut wide to reveal the adult and pet together on the riser. The pet continues its verse in a natural seated or standing pose. The adult grooves softly on screen-left.
11.5-15.0 seconds: Return to a medium two-shot. Finish the remaining audible phrase with the pet's subtle mouth movement, while the adult smiles. Use the final musical pause for a happy head tilt or small natural tail movement.

AUDIO AND MOUTH MOVEMENT
Use Audio 1 for its existing lyrics, language, vocal timing, singer handoff, rhythm, backing track and pauses. Assign the opening hook to the adult and the later verse to the pet. Match each visible mouth to its assigned reference vocal phrases and keep the music continuous through cuts. Preserve the existing wording and phrasing without additional lines, translation or narration. Produce synchronized native audio for review in the model's returned result.

QUALITY CONSTRAINTS
Keep exactly one adult, one pet and one hanging microphone. The pet retains natural animal proportions and paws throughout. Avoid human hands or a human body on the pet, copied mannequin geometry, extra animals, identity swaps, duplicate microphones, floating feet or major scene changes. Preserve realistic fur and soft studio shadows. Keep the frame free of captions, logos, watermarks and text. End at 15 seconds.

REFERENCE ROLES
@Image1 is the sole identity reference for adult performer A, who remains at screen LEFT.
@Image2 is the sole identity reference for adult performer B, who remains at screen RIGHT and is the lead vocalist.
Preserve each uploaded person's face, hair, age appearance and distinguishing features independently. Do not swap, blend or duplicate identities. Dress A in a burgundy tailored suit, white collared shirt and loosely tied burgundy necktie. Dress B in a medium-gray tailored suit with a white open-collar shirt and no tie. Adapt the outfits naturally to the uploaded adults. Keep eyewear only when present in the identity photograph.
@Image3 supplies the empty room, lighting, couch, acoustic-panel layout and microphone geometry.
@Image4 supplies the opening raised-arm pose and left/right composition near 1 second.
@Image5 supplies the shared closing hand gestures and inward lean near 9 seconds.
The smooth gray figures in Images 4 and 5 are pose guides only. Replace them completely with the realistic clothed adults from Images 1 and 2. They must never appear as mannequins or robots.
@Audio1 is the provided ten-second performance audio reference, including its existing lead vocal, beat, phrasing and supporting vocal timing.

SCENE AND CONTINUITY
A compact green-lit recording room with vertical green LED tubes, two acoustic diffuser panels, a dark green couch at the back and a plain unlettered white circular light on the rear wall. Keep exactly ONE black studio microphone on ONE straight upright floor stand between the two people, slightly in front of B. The mic, stand and room remain stationary. Both performers stand throughout, visible from the upper thighs upward with enough headroom for A's raised hand. Keep A left and B right across the entire clip; maintain the camera axis and natural proportions. Use soft frontal fill on faces with green ambient light around them.

PERFORMANCE TIMELINE
0.0-0.35s: Both adults are already beside the microphone, smiling and lightly bouncing to the beat. B starts or continues the main vocal exactly where the supplied audio starts; there is no introductory pause.
0.35-1.8s: A raises the RIGHT arm diagonally toward the upper-left of the picture, pointing one index finger upward as in Image 4. A looks toward the camera with an excited supporting expression. B keeps the lead vocal at the mic with a small natural free-hand gesture.
1.8-3.0s: A smoothly lowers the raised arm and resumes a small shoulder bounce, without changing position. B continues the lead vocal and looks forward.
3.0-6.8s: B performs compact open-hand sweeps between waist and chest height while rapping. A reacts, glances briefly toward B and returns attention to the camera. A supports the performance rather than beginning a separate solo verse.
6.8-8.2s: Both lean slightly toward the microphone, maintaining their own side. B remains the lead voice. A joins only the supporting words or accents present in the audio; otherwise A smiles or listens.
8.2-10.0s: Both make small coordinated downward/inward pointing gestures in front of their own torso, approaching the arrangement in Image 5 near 9 seconds. Keep hands separate and anatomically natural. Continue the lively performance to the end; no freeze frame or invented extra verse.

AUDIO AND MOUTH MOVEMENT
Follow Audio 1's existing wording, rhythm, music and vocal cadence as closely as the model supports. Do not translate, rewrite, slow down or add new lyrics. Align B's mouth to the dominant lead vocal. A's mouth follows only the brief supporting parts and ending participation; avoid simultaneous unrelated full verses. Keep a continuous audio bed and synchronized body accents. Identity photographs guide appearance, not voice cloning.

QUALITY
Stable realistic faces, consistent suit colors and hair, natural hands and joints, smooth transitions between the opening, middle and ending gestures, grounded body movement. No camera cuts, push-ins, zooms or close-ups. No extra people or microphones, no headphones, no desk, no ceiling-hung mic. No readable text, subtitles, lettering, show logos, brand marks or play-button awards. Do not copy the original performers' faces from pose references. Exact output duration target: 10 seconds; landscape 16:9.

kung_fu_cat_template_private_key.prompt:
Create a 9-second, 9:16 vertical photorealistic pet-comedy video. The joke is a very serious small pet performing a readable tissue-paper karate chop. Preserve the core gag, not an exact choreography from another video.

REFERENCE ROLES
@Image1 is the ONLY identity and species reference. Preserve this pet's face, eyes, muzzle, ears, fur length, coat markings, color, proportions and distinctive features. A cat stays that cat; a dog stays that dog. Do not replace it with a corgi, white cat or another animal from a source clip.
@Image2 supplies the quiet beige living room, gray rug, sofa, daylight and camera position. Ignore the background of Image1.
@Image3 is a pose-and-prop guide only: a guarded front paw, a downward paw chop, and tissue splitting at paw contact. Completely replace the smooth gray dummy with the real animal from Image1. Do not inherit the dummy's face, material, ears or body proportions. Its blank face and gray body must never appear in the result.
@Audio1 is an original nine-second action-effects reference, with short swooshes, soft impacts and paper rustles around 2.5s and 5.7s. It contains no speech or song.

SCENE AND ACTION
One pet sits upright on its haunches on the rug, with its hindquarters supported and its two front paws free for compact gestures. It remains an animal with animal paws, not a human wearing a costume. Use one continuous frontal medium shot, enough headroom and space to see the pet, forepaws and tissue. A dog may wear a plain white karate headband above its eyes; a cat can remain uncostumed. Keep eyes and ears visible. No wardrobe changes.
Only two anonymous adult hands enter from the lower edges to hold the two sides of ONE thin white tissue sheet at a time. The hands hold paper only and never pull the pet's limbs. Do not show a human face or torso.

TARGET TIMELINE
0.0-1.3s: Start directly on the pet's concentrated, comically serious stare. The hands hold an intact tissue below chest height. The pet briefly raises one forepaw into a small guard.
1.3-2.5s: A short block or feint, followed by one quick downward forepaw chop through the tissue center. The action can vary naturally with the pet's body; prioritize a clear wind-up, contact and payoff.
2.5-3.8s: At the moment the paw touches, the intact sheet splits into two fluttering sections. Show the tear visibly opening and the two held pieces separating. Keep the face recognizable. The paper does not vanish, cut itself early or remain intact after the hit.
3.8-5.7s: The hands briefly move the torn pieces out of frame and present one fresh intact tissue from below. The pet resets its guard and makes a second compact playful chop, with a second readable tear at contact near 5.7s. No extra sheets appear magically mid-frame.
5.7-7.4s: The torn halves flutter and the hands lower them. The pet gives a small triumphant paw flick or tiny shoulder bounce. A kick is optional only if natural for the uploaded animal; it must not replace the tissue-chop gag.
7.4-9.0s: Settle into a calm deadpan look toward the viewer, front paws returning to a relaxed position. Hold the comedic finish briefly without a freeze frame.

AUDIO AND QUALITY
Use the original reference effects as the timing guide, aligning paper rustles and soft impacts with the two contacts. No copied trend soundtrack, lyrics, talking, voice imitation or dramatic combat music. Keep body motion compact, playful and harmless. No injury, weapons, animal distress or fighting another animal.
Four natural limbs total; no extra paws or human fingers on the animal. Stable identity, coherent joints, connected paws, consistent fur, natural tissue physics and separated human hands. No dance replacing the chop, rapid montage, camera cuts, zoom, text, subtitles, watermarks or logos. Timing is a generation target rather than frame-exact control.

3.5-4.8s: One slow blink and a slight head tilt. Maintain the readable pads, calm expression and stable seated body. No repeated waving, lunging or aggressive claws.
4.8-6.0s: Gently draw the same paw back toward the opening position while keeping eye contact. Let the petals continue moving naturally. End on a calm, living pose; do not promise a pixel-perfect seamless loop or freeze the last frame.

AUDIO AND QUALITY
Follow the original soft effects and tap accent; keep the track gentle and speech-free. No famous melody, popular song, voice, barking or roaring. Natural animal limb count, connected joints, species-appropriate pads, stable fur and face. No human hand, extra animal, snowy transformation, costumes, text, subtitles, logos, sudden zoom, cuts or jitter. Timing is a generation target rather than exact keyframe control.
